blocking_findings.axis: wall-clock budget matching is vacuous / not measured
evidence_refs: artifacts/audit/ablation_harness.py#ee0d87a14848:82 ("wall_clock_s": WALL_CLOCK_S written as a constant on every row)
blocking_findings.finding: The acceptance requires arms matched on token AND wall-clock budgets. The simulation writes the same declared constant WALL_CLOCK_S into every row for every arm, so check_budget_match's wall-clock clause always sees a 0% spread. A 10x wall-clock divergence between arms could not be detected by this pipeline as written. The design's falsifier 'arms not matched within 2% on wall-clock -> comparison void' therefore cannot fire. Matching must be measured per arm (e.g. per-arm elapsed wall time under a simulated concurrency/latency model) before the design can claim the axis is controlled.

blocking_findings.axis: declared matched fields are not measured or recorded
evidence_refs: evaluation/ablation_design.yaml#1b2a83ef670b:49 (rule: "Verifier calls per accepted artifact and human-review minutes are also equalised")
artifacts/audit/ablation_harness.py#ee0d87a14848:42-43 (VERIFIER_CALLS_PER_ACCEPT = 3, HUMAN_REVIEW_MINUTES = 30 are declared constants and never emitted into any row or summary)
evaluation/ablation_dryrun_report.json#e1860fa1c6ce (no verifier_calls or human_review field anywhere in the report)
blocking_findings.finding: Two of the four fields the design declares as matched are never measured: verifier_calls_per_accepted_artifact and human_review_minutes are module constants (3, 30) that appear in no CSV row, no per-arm summary, and no budget check. The design's own text says they are equalised; the pipeline cannot demonstrate this, and cost_per_accepted_artifact is specified in the design as a three-component secondary metric ([tokens, agent_hours, verifier_calls]) while the report emits only cost_per_accepted_tokens. At minimum the design should mark these two fields as declared-but-not-enforced, or the harness should emit and check them.

blocking_findings.axis: the named canonical harness is not the one that produced the dry-run, and its tolerance is looser than the design's rule
evidence_refs: evaluation/ablation_design.yaml#1b2a83ef670b:47-48 (rule: same token budget B +/-2% and wall-clock T +/-2%)
evaluation/ablation_harness.py#df878e97bf6e:430-467 (load_design + run_ablation; the design file sets no token_tolerance, so the 15% default survives)
blocking_findings.finding: Two harness copies exist with different hashes and different enforcement. The design names artifacts/audit/ablation_harness.py, which delegates to audit_lib.check_budget_match at tol=0.02 and so agrees with the +/-2% rule; the dry-run numbers were clearly produced by that copy. But evaluation/ablation_harness.py is a second copy whose own budget checker runs at token_tolerance=0.15, and loading the pinned design into it does not change that (the design sets no token_tolerance key). Any future run through the evaluation/ copy would accept a token spread in (2%, 15%] that the design explicitly forbids - a silent violation of HF-11 / the H-design falsifier. The two copies must be reconciled to one canonical harness, or the design must pin the tolerance in the design file itself and name only the canonical path.

non_blocking_findings.finding: The second harness copy (evaluation/ablation_harness.py) has no --execute provider guard at all; the canonical copy refuses without SWARM_PROVIDERS. If the evaluation/ copy is ever treated as authoritative, the fail-closed property in the design (execution_status.blocker) is not enforced by that file. Low risk today because nothing executed, but it is the same divergence as B3.

The dry-run report carries no generator_sha256 or harness_version, so the report cannot be tied to the harness revision that produced it; the evaluation/ copy's own report schema does emit generator_sha256. Provenance of the dry run should be recorded in the report (harness path + sha256), especially since two copies exist.

Metric-name drift: the design's secondary list names information_gain and duplication as kish_ess-based; the canonical report emits kish_ess_reviewers and mean_novelty but no information_gain field. The eight pre-registered harness metrics and the design's eight metrics are not a 1:1 named mapping. Harmless for a dry run, but the pre-registration should use identical names so the eventual primary analysis cannot be re-scoped after seeing results.

The NULL arm is declared honestly as not-implemented-as-designed: the report's null_arm_note states the simulation uses a declared low-acceptance arm instead of iid random selection from the candidate pool at matched tokens. This is correctly labelled, but the design's H-swarm falsifier compares ICC-IC against 'the NULL spread'; until the NULL arm is a real iid candidate-pool draw with its own spread estimate, that falsifier is not yet executable.

The guardrail example fires on the simulation's own declared inputs: hard_failure_rate is 0.1652 (IC) and 0.1518 (NULL), above the 0.10 truncation rule, with ICC at 0.0983 - marginally inside. The dry run therefore shows that under the declared rates the treatment arm sits one step below the guardrail and two arms are truncated. That is a useful design signal (the guardrail is binding), not a defect, but the power/decision narrative should state that the primary comparison may exclude truncated arms by construction.

criteria_detail.class_leakage: N/A - A2 is GLOBAL (design/methodology), not one of the four frozen physics classes. The design's task suite T1-T4 is class-bound by construction and names all four frozen classes (harness CLASSES matches evaluation_rubric.yaml frozen_classes).
criteria_detail.conclusion_inflation: none observed - the artifact claims design + simulated pipeline only; execution_status.state = blocked and what_is_not_done explicitly disclaims any real arm execution. No theorem/result claim is made.
criteria_detail.assumption_completeness: the power warning is honest and correct (n=8 cannot detect the ~3% offline effect; 1378 outputs needed for 5pt). The main completeness gap is that two declared matched fields are not measured (B2).
criteria_detail.decidable_falsifier: the design's falsifier_of_this_design list is decidable in principle, but the wall-clock item is not decidable against this pipeline (B1) and the NULL-spread item is not yet executable (N4).
criteria_detail.two_readers_disagree: the field most likely to draw disagreement is matched_fields (line 58), which asserts four matched quantities while only two are checked; a second reader could reasonably accept the design on the token result alone. This is why the blocking findings are scoped to that field and to the harness divergence rather than to the whole design.
